entries.body: 3½ months sitting in Opua! Thomas hurt himself windsurfing at Urupukapuka — the prettiest spot in the Bay of Islands. You could actually see the bottom there! We hung out in Opua so he could go to the doctor. Big strain in his hip joint — only time could cure it. Then I got another job doing web pages for Bob & Masae Seige, the Bay of Islands Travel Information Network. But we are finally on our way to South Minerva Reef. Nice 15 kt southerly breeze, but it is cold! Goodbye New Zealand — it was an interesting time!
entries.conditions: Departed Opua bound for South Minerva Reef. Wind: 15 kt southerly; cold.

entries.body: Last night was beautiful, full moon, light SE winds, the boat roaring along at 6 knots! But of course it didn't last and now we are getting ready to tack, 3 pm and the wind turned NE. Oh well, we knew it wouldn't be easy. Thomas has been seasick all day so I have had to do the deck work. Well we just tacked and of course the wind turned back SE, so we tacked again. Forgot what a pain in the ass sailing is! We had fun in Opua. Met Sharon & Steve on Poet's Place again, I took a lot of long walks with her and got to know her. Saw Infidean again briefly, Athenor showed up the last 2 weeks we were there. Really enjoyed Capaz — Rob, Sharin, and their 3 boys Brian, Scott, and Chris. Of course Brian became big buddies with them. I got into fixing laptop computers for the German/Swiss sailors and was a lot busier than I really cared to be. Leo on Moonlight was there, took us to Whangarei once, Rolf on Yelo let us borrow his car several times. But Sharon was the most generous, always taking people along with her. Finally met George & Lorraine on Silent Runner, who we had seen in Bora Bora. Sharon organized lots of pot luck movie nights at the Opua Cruising Club which were big fun. That was our main entertainment while we were there. I got to surf the net every day at work and bought a digital camera and another laptop on EBay. Thomas worked on the boat, time passed, and it got colder.
entries.conditions: Wind: SE then NE then back SE; tacking. 24-hour run — 135 miles.

entries.body: It was a boisterous night, had to put in reefs, set the yankee jib. Now we're banging along, relatively comfortably, as long as we lie down! 30 knots of wind, close reaching, heading just to windward of our course. Everyone is over their seasickness. But the sun is shining, the squalls are through, it's just trade winds.
entries.conditions: Wind: 30 knots, close reaching. 24-hour run — 113 miles.

entries.body: Can't say this is comfortable but we are sailing in the right direction, still making easting from the rhumb line, anticipating a NE wind shift. Squally weather, 25–30 SE, making around 5 knots. We spent most of yesterday sleeping, not much else to do. Brian ended up on the floor last night after fighting with his bed and losing. Charlotte is happy with just a reefed mizzen and yankee — we sure are glad to have the 2nd forestay with the fitting we had welded to the bowsprit in Opua. The sail is almost new and flies beautifully. Brian is a good sailor, he takes the boredom, bland food, discomfort, with cheer.
entries.conditions: Wind: SE 25–30, squally; around 5 knots. 24-hour run — 125 miles.

entries.body: The wind keeps slowly turning north — kind of frustrating. We can handle the discomfort, the wetness, but to have to heave to will be a real bummer. Presently we are still slogging along, just barely on course. At least we got to shower and wash our hair. Except for Brian, who vows not to wash until we reach port! Charlotte is doing okay with staysail, double-reefed main and mizzen. Intermittent sun, not too squally yet.
entries.conditions: Wind: slowly turning north. 24-hour run — 138 miles.

entries.body: Wind turned NE last night, we are making very little easting now. Will need a favorable wind shift to get to South Minerva. Woke up to 30–35, very rough. Got the main down, been riding relatively comfortably with the boat closed up, no looking around today! We are all reading, nothing to do but keep still. Oh isn't it fun!
entries.conditions: Wind: NE, 30–35, very rough. 24-hour run — 125 miles.

entries.body: It's only gotten worse — total cloud cover, squally all last night and today, put another reef in the mizzen. The boat is not slamming so much now. We are still heading due north, so will miss Minerva Reef. Too bad — Capaz made it in this morning, we would like to be comfortably anchored! Instead we will have to continue on to Fiji. All the other boats are hove to. It's not really that bad! Heavy weather is boring. I had to sew the bimini top — a seam had come undone. We got Brian to wash a little bit.
entries.conditions: Total cloud cover, squally, heading due north. 24-hour run — 100 miles.

entries.body: The gnarly weather is finally through! The squalls were less violent and shorter last night and this morning we were able to set the yankee. Passed South Minerva reef this morning, 35 miles to the west, and talked to Gene on Reflections. So we will carry on to Savu Savu. Heading due north, some sunshine today, hardly any squalls. It was nice to talk to someone else we knew after being alone out here for a week. I took a nice rainwater shower this morning — it is much warmer. Back to shorts and T shirts. It would have been nice to stop though, the boat is an awful mess.
entries.conditions: Passed South Minerva Reef 35 miles to the west; heading due north for Savusavu. 24-hour run — 110 miles.

entries.body: Still squally, main up and main down, but the sun is out and we seem to be through the worst of the front. Talked to Capaz this morning, the boys were missing Brian. We wanted to stop so bad, have time to clean up, get ready for Fiji, oh well. The boat is an absolute slime pit. But it is hot! We are lolling around in no shirts. Every towel on the boat is wet with sea water. And we'll get there on the weekend and have to hide from customs til Monday. Seems like I wrote the same thing yesterday! Got an email from Sharon — Poet's Place — about how awful the 30-hour flight back to Seattle was — little does she know! Charlotte can handle this!
entries.conditions: Wind 20 knots, seas 3 meter swell, maintaining 5 knots to windward still. 24-hour run — 120 miles.

entries.body: Land ho! We spotted the first Fijian island a while ago. We will pass it by sunset, then sail between islands all night. Will arrive in Savu Savu tomorrow sundown. It's a nice day, 15–20 knots, lots of sun, still going into it, but the big ocean swell is gone — there are islands way to windward. We are happy with Charlotte — maintaining 5 knots to windward in big seas!
entries.conditions: Wind: 15–20 knots; 5 knots to windward. Landfall — first Fijian island sighted. 24-hour run — 135 miles.

entries.body: Good day! Thought we would have a nice calm sail last night, wind and seas were down, had full sails up. Caught a 4-ft Mahi mahi just before sunset. Brian got it in with the new gaff — easier than using a spear gun! So they ate well last night. I'm getting kind of tired of bread, cheese, and peanut butter! Then the wind died around 9 pm. We motored some past a long-liner fishing boat, but drifted most of the night. Wind came up this morning around 11, we have been sailing slowly but comfortably all day. I got to clean up and do some laundry! So we aren't anchored in Savusavu yet, no big deal, everyone is content on board. Been playing with the digital camera, doing email, Brian is busy with the electronic organizer Thomas gave him. We got last week's email finally — the renters paid so life is good again! No hurry to get to harbor, it's weekend now.
entries.conditions: Wind died ~9 pm, motored/drifted overnight, wind back ~11 am. 24-hour run — 90 miles.

entries.body: It was a beautiful night — millions of stars, a nice 10 knot breeze, no ships in sight. We have enjoyed sailing in the Koro Sea. At sunrise we were 20 miles south of Savusavu. Took till 1 pm to get to anchor. It is incredible — reminds us of French Polynesia. White beaches, lots of swaying palm trees, lush green hills, clear blue water. And the water is warm! On the water is the place to be in Fiji, as the air is hot. Will take some getting used to. Everyone is happy with a good successful voyage complete. It's great to be cruising again!
entries.conditions: 10-knot breeze; at sunrise 20 miles south of Savusavu. Voyage from New Zealand completed.

entries.body: Left Cousteau anchorage near Savusavu at 6 am — motor-sailing 40 miles to windward. It was not pleasant! Thought about turning around a few times, but once we got in the lee of Taveuni, the wind dropped. Met Capaz and chugged into Viani Anchored Monday, spent a few busy days digging around in Savusavu, taking the boys to the hotel pools, socializing. It was hot! Now we are in Viani Bay, enroute to the Exploring Isles. Water is pleasant, good swimming, catching up on boat chores, relaxing after that rough passage! We are pleased with how Charlotte handled the heavy weather — most other boats had a lot more problems. It's great to be back in the tropics!
entries.conditions: 40 miles to windward, motorsailing into the lee of Taveuni. Now at Viani Bay, enroute to the Exploring Isles.

entries.body: Time passed quickly in Viani Bay. We enjoyed meeting Jack Fisher, the official greeter, and his family Sophie, Elizabeth and Tiare. We took a hike, slogging through the mud, to a vegetable farm and bought some food picked fresh off the plants. The Capaz family got to try out our windsurfers. We relaxed! Today it's back beating to windward under motor, not bad until we rounded the north cape of Taveuni and little trades head on. We hated it. But like all unpleasant situations, it came to an end, and now we are alone, with Capaz, outside Matagi Island in a small cove on the north shore. Nice snorkeling right in the anchorage. Caught a wahoo coming in and had a barbeque on Capaz last night. Very green, smells earthy here.
entries.conditions: Motored north around the cape of Taveuni to Matagi Island; little trades head on.

entries.body: Matagi was nice, quiet, good snorkeling. We had a great beach pot luck last night, with a bright half moon, nice fire, Rob & Vivian H playing guitar. The other boys buried Scott and gave him a big set of boobs! Today, hoping for light NE winds, we left at 4 am for Vanua Balavu, 50 miles to windward. Of course the wind went SE and picked up, we were bashing again, just what we wanted to avoid. It was kind of miserable at times. But then we went into the lee of an island and managed to get some windward miles. Came in just an hour after Capaz! It's beautiful here, totally landlocked harbor, 6 other boats. Brian's birthday tomorrow — it's been a fun 12 years with him. We remember his birth and how perfect he was. Now he's almost as big as me, strong, well-muscled, a good-looking boy. Happy birthday, buddy!
entries.conditions: 50 miles to windward, Matagi to Vanua Balavu. Wind: hoped-for NE went SE and built; bashing.

entries.body: It was a fun 2 weeks out at Vanua Balavu. We stayed a week at the plantation. Went to the village to do sevu-sevu, no big deal. The men went diving out on the reef several times, got lots of lobster. Got some soursop and coconuts from the locals. We had cake and movies for Brian's birthday. He got a Celtic necklace and some Gameboy games from Capaz. Did a bit of hiking but it was always muddy. Then we moved over to the Bay of Islands — very pretty — lots of little rocky islands but nowhere to go to store. Infidean with Rick, Patty and Jesse joined us for a few days and we had daily pot luck dinners. Took Capaz out to the reef on a couple of calm days and the reefs were fantastic out there. It was a nice place but we were missing beaches, so today we are doing an overnighter to Dravuni at Kadavu. A bit too windy, just forward of the beam, not what we really wanted!
entries.conditions: Departing Vanua Balavu on an overnighter to Dravuni, Kadavu. Wind: too windy, just forward of the beam.

entries.body: It piped up at sundown last night — up to 28 knots according to Rob. We had to reef down but Charlotte was flying — over 7 knots, must have been current. The seas were very confused. No sleeping — too many noises! Sailed into the Great Astrolabe Reef — about 4 pm. It sure is nice here — lots of beaches! The locals remember Capaz and are happy to see them. I had a remora try to attach to me when I went swimming — yuck!
entries.conditions: Wind up to 28 knots, confused seas; reefed down, 7 knots. We did 145 miles in 24 hours. Arrived the Great Astrolabe Reef ~4 pm.

entries.body: So we have been 2 weeks in the Kadavu — Astrolabe Reef area. Rob organized a pig roast at Dravuni last week that was great fun — 4 boats with kids, the extended family he knows there. We really enjoyed our time on Yaukuve, a deserted island with a nice sandy beach. The kids built a big hut out of palm fronds and spent 2 nights sleeping ashore. We had beach bonfires several nights. Met Libby Lane with Drew, Monique and 11-year-old twins Grace & Celeste, and English Make Time with Jeff, Penny, and daughters Estrel and Hayley, they are lots of fun! After Capaz moved on, we moved to Buliya and then to a bay on the south corner of Kadavu. Pretty bay, very dramatic, but no shore access, all mangroves. It rained and blew for several days and [we] have been stuck on the boat. Now we are at Ono, planning to go to Suva tomorrow.
entries.conditions: At Ono, planning to sail to Suva tomorrow.

entries.body: What a ride to Suva! We were on a broad reach — 30 knots — reefed main and reefed mizzen, doing 7 knots. It was boisterous but over quickly. Now we are in the big city, spending money. Doesn't look that inviting but the fresh fruits & vegetables are good!
entries.conditions: Broad reach, 30 knots, reefed; 7 knots. Arrived Suva.

entries.body: Time to get out of Suva — we spent lots of money, got what we needed — new printer for $50 US, a set of big wrenches for Thomas, new binoculars. We enjoyed the street food, loaded the boat with fruits & vegetables, saw Terminator III at the movie theater. Disappointment was not meeting any new people. Royal Suva Yacht Club was a bore. Got hit with more wind than we expected today, on a 30-mile sail out to Beqa. Wind kept picking up, under bare poles for a while! At least it is off the wind. Anchored in the harbor, feeling extremely wind blown, finally got the anchor to stick. It is very gusty here but there is nowhere else to go. Caught a big golden Dorado!
entries.conditions: 30-mile sail Suva to Beqa. Wind built; under bare poles for a while; very gusty anchorage.

entries.body: Out of that hole! We were heeled over half the time at anchor, gusts up to 50 knots, no fun at all. I did get in a swim yesterday, between rain squalls. Would have liked to visit the village, but it was too windy to launch the dinghy. It gusted 40 or more as we pulled up the anchor, motored the 4 miles out to the reef. Once on course downwind, with just a staysail, it is quite comfortable. Heading for Vunaniu harbor, hoping for a calm anchorage for a change!
entries.conditions: Gusts to 50 knots at anchor, 40+ pulling up; downwind under staysail to Vunaniu.

entries.body: Well it was a very comfortable night, totally calm, not much wind, what a change! Today the sun is hot, the wind is light, from the north. We are sailing with 2 other boats who were in Suva and spent the night with us. Just puttering along, enjoying the sunshine. Will stop in Natadola harbor, looks like it has a nice long beach.
entries.conditions: Calm; light north wind. Sailing to Natadola harbor.

entries.body: What an awful night! We rolled nonstop, no sleep. But we had a nice walk on the beach last night and Brian got to ride a horse. We met Ithaca with Mike and Marguerite, who we had seen since Suva. Today is great sailing, wind south of east, downwind along the SW coast of Viti Levu. We sailed in the reef entrance, flying at 6½ knots. The west coast is much drier but also sunnier. Musket Cove is not exactly a protected anchorage, rather open to the south, 50 ft deep, but holding seems to be good. Very beautiful, lots of white sand beaches, lots of wind, lots of boats!
entries.conditions: Wind south of east; downwind along the SW coast of Viti Levu at 6½ knots to Musket Cove.

entries.body: Four weeks in Nadi waters — it sure went fast! We had fun in Musket Cove. Thomas had wild windsurfing for a week, Brian and I did some too. Brian hung out with the girls on Libby Lane, also met Soleka, English Marten, Katherine, & 8-year-old Will aboard. Took a trip to Lautoka to go shopping and eat more cheap Indian street food. Got some projects done on the boat. Infidean showed up just when we were ready to leave Fiji, had a couple of nice evenings with them. One more run to Lautoka to check out, then a couple of nights in Saweni Bay, then one last night at Musket when the wind died. It was very pretty there, great salt-water pool with 25 meter lap lanes, lots of walking, palm trees, white sand, blue water. The sun shone every day! But it's time to move on, light winds, to Vanuatu. We will have good memories of Fiji — the stark coastal scenery, lush mangrove bays with deep green water, and the perfect tropical offshore islands. Challenging sailing — many cruisers ended up on reefs. Today we motored out the reef cut, then were becalmed. Motored until I had had enough of it, then the wind came up right after I shut it down! Sailing with lots of different sails — mizzen drifter, poled-out genoa, main & staysail.
entries.conditions: After four weeks in Nadi waters. Departed for Vanuatu; motored out the reef cut, becalmed, then wind filled in. Sailing under mizzen drifter, poled-out genoa, main & staysail.

entries.body: Nice night, although a bit rolly, had to do some sail changes in the middle of the night, mostly downwind but shifty. Running nicely now with 4 sails up — yankee instead of staysail, mizzen drifter pulling well. 10–12 knots of easterly winds. A bit slow at times, but maintaining 4–5 knots. We passed a 40-ft cutter, almost keeping up with Silent Runner, George & Lorraine. All in all quite pleasant! Did catch a nice mahi this morning.
entries.conditions: Wind: easterly 10–12 knots, shifty downwind; 4 sails up; 4–5 knots.

entries.body: Oops — missed yesterday! It wasn't much — Brian & I started school, had a big fight over math, but the new science & social studies went well. Wind was very light from the east, then turned NE in the middle of the night. We were sailing beautifully to windward for a while, 5–6 knots in a flat calm sea. Then today we sailed under a cloud line and the wind turned west, very light. We motored for several hours, now hove to until something changes. Too bad — only 130 miles to go to Vila. It's not uncomfortable out here, no storms to fight. So we will sit here for now.
entries.conditions: Wind: light east → NE → SW → west; 5–6 knots then motoring. 130 miles to go to Vila.

entries.body: Happy birthday Thomas! 15 knots headwinds and we are tacking, bashing into the seas and making very little progress. Charlotte is not a particularly happy boat today. Otherwise the weather is fine, nice sunny day. Lost two fish, one a nice mahi. Guess we'll be out here forever.
entries.conditions: Wind: 15 knots head winds; tacking, little progress.

entries.body: Well we did about 40 miles yesterday, tacking nonstop. Got tired of it this morning, winds are lighter, can't hold a decent course, extremely frustrated. Did catch a big bull dolphin this morning, one bright spot in the day! Finally broke down and tried motoring, but it's hopeless — only 3.5 knots made good. Don't understand how all these other people can motor for days on end. The wind is supposed to come up tomorrow — we can only hope.
entries.conditions: ~40 miles made good tacking; lighter winds; motoring only 3.5 knots made good.

entries.body: The wind turned last night for 3 hours! We were so happy, the boat was sailing so nice! It did finally come to the south this morning and we sailed slowly, watching Efate get bigger. Great day, lots of sunshine. We will be in just after dark tonight. Everyone is happier, anticipating landfall. It was a long trip.
entries.conditions: Wind turned south; sailing slowly toward landfall. Arriving just after dark.

entries.body: A quick week in Vila as usual. Anchored at 8 pm near the quarantine buoy — the map was right on. Silent Runner didn't show up for two days — their transmission had broken again and they hove to, rather than tacked. Guess we didn't do so bad after all. Lots of people here we know — Rolf with Daniella on Yelo and best of all Desert Rose with Mick, Lynne, Teddo, Edwina & Issy. We hung out with them a year ago in Tonga. Had some fun evenings with them. also saw Onyx, Tranquility, Sayo, Gitano, Sojourner. Met a nice older Aussie couple, Iris & Graham on Time Wise. Brian got quite friendly with Iris and I got [Chip] going on her XP laptop with USB interface. Thomas enjoyed eating cheap tender steak, we shopped for DVDs and duty free liquor. No other bargains here — food in the supermarkets costs twice as much as Fiji. We attended a local play showing the history of Vanuatu. Had a really good time in general, Brian was happy to see the Desert Rose kids again. But it's a city, so Saturday, after we got our Australian visas (what a hassle — my last name, Brian's new passport, they were confused by the situation but finally gave in as we had all important documentation) we moved, with Desert Rose and Time Wise to Mele Bay 5 miles away. There we decided with Fidelio & Alderan to do an overnighter to Epi. Ian is usually good with the weather. He predicted a restful night, but that was not the case. We flew north in 20–25 knots SE on the beam, had to keep shortening sail to slow the boat down. Dawn found us 6 miles from Lamen Bay, and the wind died then turned NE. We were happy to get the hook down, not much rest last night. There is a resident dugong in the Bay and lots of loggerhead turtles.
entries.conditions: Anchored Port Vila near quarantine buoy; later Mele Bay, then overnight to Lamen Bay, Epi. Wind: SE 20–25 on the beam, then died / NE at dawn.

entries.body: Bunches of boats in Lamen Bay that we have met before — Fidelio, Time Wise, Irish Alderan, some others. We swam with the dugong and got to pet him and ride on him (kind of!) Had a birthday dinner with Time Wise. Thomas and Brian gave me some beautiful earrings made of red coral and mother of pearl. Thomas was just recovering from a stomach bug, then Brian & I got it on Wednesday. I was awfully sick. What a 50th birthday — I will not forget it. Had to spend the day at anchor until we recovered. We are feeling better today, light wind, so we set sail for the Maskelyne Islands off the coast of Malekula. Before we got there we had head winds! Pulled into a very nice snug little anchorage at Awei Island, home of the magic weather stones — pieces of quartz that give off blue sparks when you strike them together, and cause thunder storms. It is very calm and peaceful here, surrounded by mangroves, tiny sand beaches, shy natives paddling beautiful dugout canoes with proas. It is easy to trade old clothes for fruit.
entries.conditions: Lamen Bay, Epi; later Awei Island, Maskelyne Islands. Light wind after illness.

entries.body: Quiet day on Awei anchorage yesterday. We launched the dinghy in late afternoon and looked for the magic quartz rocks on the beach. We found a number of interesting, reddish & blueish quartz stones, some green stones, some white quartz. Had to order Brian not to strike them together! Left today originally for Ambrym, but the wind was easterly and it was a bit of a beat. After much indecision, we set course for Crab Bay on Malekula, and down wind. Brian and I are both still feeling a bit under. Great sail in 20 knots along the coast. The volcano at Ambrym was spitting clouds of smoke & dust. Entered a nice little cove with a beautiful long sandy beach. I'll rest here for a day!
entries.conditions: Wind: easterly beat toward Ambrym abandoned; downwind to Crab Bay, Malekula, ~20 knots.

entries.body: Met some nice kiwis in Crab Bay — they actually came over to visit! Took a walk on the long sand beach, I saw a lion fish snorkeling in the shallows. I'm a bit nervous about swimming in Vanuatu — too many stories of tiger shark attacks! 40 miles to go today to Santo today and we are drifting in light winds, slowly heading north. It is peaceful out there at least! The air is very hazy, can barely see any other islands.
entries.conditions: Departing Crab Bay for Santo; light winds, drifting north. ~40 miles.

entries.body:
Just a few quick days in Luganville. Nice anchorage off the beach by the Beach Front Resort, nice Aussie folks running it. I finally saw a doctor and he said I have dengue fever. It explains my fatigue over the past month! Lucky I am almost over it, just need to be careful, take it easy, not get bitten by a mosquito! Thomas scuba dove the President Coolidge, an intact WWII wreck in 120 feet of water. He liked it, but it was very dark down there! Left town yesterday morning to do an overnighter to Waterfall Bay, Vanua Lava, Banks Islands, where a festival is being held. Great sailing day, wind a bit light from the SE, broad reaching at 4½ knots. Wind turned twice during the night to NE, picked up, then died. Anchored by 9 am in Waterfall Bay — incredibly beautiful spot! There are 2 waterfalls cascading down the cliff side. The local villagers are so happy to see us! Our t-shirt stash will go fast here.

Saw Yelo with Rolf & Daniella again in Santo, saw Mangwana (the Mongols) again, met Fay & Ingrid on Moon Penny.
entries.conditions: Luganville then overnight to Waterfall Bay, Vanua Lava. Wind: light SE, 4½ knots; NE overnight.

entries.body:
Had a great time at the festival in Waterfall Bay. The winds were light while we were there, the weather hot & sunny, 15 boats showed up. Yelo came, we spent a lot of time with them. Met Ophelia, [uncertain: Hans], Eva and little Lola. Thomas took lots of great pictures. Jimmy, a local, invited us to a meal at his house — sweet potato laplap was surprisingly good, fresh water prawns cooked with green onions, and cassava. They build beautiful huts from palm and bamboo with woven walls in different designs, palm thatch roofs, little windows covered with pieces of bamboo. Very airy and comfortable! On the floor they put coral rubble to keep the sand down. Jimmy had a hand made table and benches, woven mats on the floor. His entire family sat on the floor and watched us while we ate.

The festival was a lot of fun, very intimate with only a few locals. [uncertain: Henaki] was inaugurated as the first blood chief in 90 years. They killed a pig — quite humanely by poisoning it with an arrow before beating it to death. All the members of his extended family were anointed with pig blood on the temples. Lots of dancing and singing. The men & women all wore grass skirts. The snake dance with the men painted to look like black & white coral snakes was cool. The 2nd day they prepared a traditional feast using all old methods, scraping coconut with clam shells, cooking prawns and fish in pieces of hollow bamboo on hot stones. They ground fresh kava root with a piece of coral. Their kava bowls were made from plastic fishing floats — not exactly traditional! The last day we climbed to the top of the waterfall and heard the women making water music with their hands and arms. None of the white women could do it! It was all very interesting, but we were exhausted from being on shore all day. Sailed to the Reef Islands today.
entries.conditions: Waterfall Bay festival, Vanua Lava; light winds, hot & sunny. Sailed to the Reef Islands.

entries.body: We left the Reef Islands with regret, were tired of the constant wind blowing 25 knots. It was beautiful there, white powdery sand beach on the island, crystal clear water. Unfortunately the anchorage was exposed, behind the reef, and the island was a half-mile dingy ride away. Had a great time windsurfing, Brian graduated to my rig, and was very good. Namirda was there, Niel & Greta are good wind surfers. Mangwana came in and the boys were kite surfing. We spent most afternoons on the beach hanging out with the other cruisers, enjoying the beach, getting out of the strong wind. Fast windy passage down to Waterfall Bay today, fill up on water, get some fresh fruit.
entries.conditions: Reef Islands; wind 25 knots. Fast windy return to Waterfall Bay.

entries.body: Too much politics in Waterfall Bay, the chiefs are arguing with each other, but we did get bananas, papayas, grapefruit and pumpkin from both of them. Had dinner with Kerely last night. It is very windy today, we are hard on it, bashing down to Gaua, no fun at all! But Charlotte is doing great, going high to windward, 5 knots average in 25 knots of wind. Four other boats heading to the same anchorage.
entries.conditions: Waterfall Bay to Gaua. Wind: 25 knots, hard on it; 5 knots average.

entries.body:
Much more pleasant sailing today! The village at Gaua was very poor, but I did score a nice carving there. We took an extremely strenuous hike to the lakes in the middle of the island with Namirda, 7 hours of hiking total. We barely made it back, the boys got us some coconuts that rejuvenated us. We were the big attraction in the village. The hike through the jungle was interesting, no birds, no wildlife, lots of vines to trip over, We passed steaming mud pools. The lake itself was quite hot along the edges and the water was shallow and warm. We rested for an hour on the hot stones along the shoreline and enjoyed the solitude. The walk back was a nightmare, everyone was sore. Got a cool carving from the village.

Today there are 3 other boats out here, Namirda, Alderan and Flight of Time, all going to Santo. The winds are much lighter, we are close reaching, quite pleasant for a change.
entries.conditions: Gaua crater-lakes hike; then sailing toward Santo. Winds lighter, close reaching.

entries.body: Really enjoyed Port Orly. The island we anchored behind was deserted, with a fresh water lake for swimming and laundry. It was pretty and peaceful there. Good swimming, nice beach. Had dinner on Alderan and invited them over for a movie. Today we are going somewhere, weren't sure, depended on how the wind blew. Ended up in Peterson Bay, met Namirda, Pacific Bliss (another cat like Yelo) with Gunther & Lois aboard, and Fidelio. Caught a large mahi which we shared with our friends in return for cold beers — good trade! Nice anchorage behind the reef here.
entries.conditions: Port Olry (written Port Orly) then Peterson Bay, Santo.

entries.body: Decided to run to Loganville this afternoon, hit the stores and the market tomorrow morning for supplies. Had a nice sail around the corner and all the way to the anchorage. Lots of boats in Loganville.
entries.conditions: Peterson Bay to Luganville (written Loganville).

entries.body: Wanted to head over to Ambae this morning for the festival at Lolowai, but the wind is nonexistent. Instead, we stopped with Alderan at Million Dollar Point and had a great snorkel. US dumped a lot of their leftover stuff in the ocean here rather than leave it to the islanders. There were numerous ships, pieces of jeeps, a fork lift, all covered with coral. It was a fun dive. Then we continued around the corner and anchored in Palikulo Bay. Time Wise was there, we enjoyed a potluck dinner together.
entries.conditions: Million Dollar Point snorkel; anchored Palikulo Bay. Wind nonexistent for Ambae.

entries.body: Boisterous sail to Ambae today! We are out here with 3 other boats, Charlotte is keeping up in speed and pointing to windward. It is an awful rough slog, gusts to 30 knots, burying the bow to the mast at times, way overpowered with the reefed genoa. But we make it, averaging 5 knots! The anchorage at Lolowai is cute, surrounded on 3 sides by rock cliffs, with a narrow shallow entrance. We meet Explorer here with Bob & Hella, hadn't seen them since the Galapagos. Tevaki Nui is here with their 8-year-old girl, Brian is not thrilled unfortunately.
entries.conditions: Santo to Lolowai, Ambae. Gusts to 30 knots; averaging 5 knots.

entries.body: Loved the festival — it was a 20-minute truck ride up in the hills in a big grassy meadow surrounded by huge banyan and mango trees. The dancing was very colorful and quite powerful at times. The dancers here wear colored mats — a diaper for the men, 2 wraps for the women — skirt & bodice. Lots of chiefs dressed in full regalia, dancing to show their approval of the presentations. 15 or more boats here, including Tranquility with Rick & Mary, Silverfin with Carl & Kathleen, others. It is a good time. It's nice to get away from the ocean and hang out in a cool green spot all day. We picked up some really different baskets, a chief staff for Brian with a spear point tip. We liked the peace and enclosedness of the anchorage and the snorkeling, but decided to move over to Maewo today, 8 miles to an anchorage that I heard was nice. Easy sail for a change, but that's because it's so early in the morning, before the trades pick up. We are at Narovorovo or something like that and the locals are listening to loud reggae music at 9 am!
entries.conditions: Lolowai festival, Ambae; then 8 miles to Narovorovo, Maewo.

entries.body: Had a great time in Narovorovo — what a tongue twister!) Met the Peace Corps worker, Jamie, and his girlfriend Valerie, fixed his XP laptop that was crashed. He took us to the waterfall, along with Kathleen & Carl on Silverfin, very hot walk. I did my laundry at the village spigot, got to meet the shy but friendly villagers. We were only the 4th boat to stop there. It was a pleasant interlude. This morning we punched down to Asanvari, where there is a 'Yacht Club' hosted by Chief Nelson. Really glad we came to Maewo!
entries.conditions: Narovorovo to Asanvari, Maewo.

entries.body: Asanvari had a picture-perfect village and a nice view of the channel across to Pentecost, but it was too nice, they are too used to having cruisers there. We did trade for some more baskets, now we have lots of presents! Took a great snorkel in clear water, saw big groupers and a family of eagle rays. I did my laundry at the waterfall, very convenient! Today we left at 4am, hoping for a good wind to blow us the [illegible] miles to Luganville. Instead, we got barely 10 knots, a slow but pleasant trip, made it in 13 hours, right to the anchorage. We are next to Alderan again!
entries.conditions: Asanvari to Luganville in 13 hours. Wind: barely 10 knots.
